waterways.

Wilmington.

possible.

properties.description:
We will continue to some light rain or snow in the lower
elevations with little or no snow accumulation overnight, but the
higher elevations especially above 2500 feet will be primarily
snow overnight into Friday morning. While the ground is warm, some
of the higher terrain of the Plateau, southwest Virginia, the
east Tennessee mountains, and the mountains of southwest North
Carolina will see around an inch of snow accumulation. A few
mountain peaks may see accumulations in the 2 to 3 inch range.

While the ground is still fairly warm this early in the season,
be alert for slippery spots on roadways if traveling in these
areas, especially on bridges and overpasses.

Please plan accordingly if planning to travel in or through these
areas.  Using extra caution is advised, slow down, and allow
extra distance between yourself and other vehicles.

Tennessee border and across Macon and northern Jackson counties
overnight. By Friday morning, snowfall of 1 to 2 inches, with
locally higher amounts is possible across the higher elevations of
western Graham and western Macon Counties, as well as the higher
elevations of the Smokies. A dusting to up to an inch is possible
across the upslope areas of the Northern Mountains. The snow may
briefly mix with light freezing rain or drizzle before ending
Friday morning. While a brief period of wintry weather is possible
in the valleys across the Tennessee border counties Friday
morning, little-to-no accumulation is expected in these areas.

North Carolina tonight or Friday morning should plan for potential
slick spots on roads.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 26 at 9:52PM EST by NWS Peachtree City GA
properties.description:
Light rain transitioning to light snow has begun in areas across
north Georgia this evening as expected. Temperatures below
approximately 2500' remain just at or above freezing, meaning
no significant accumulations are expected but snow could briefly
linger on elevated or grassy surfaces through the night. Above
2500' temperatures have fallen to at or below freezing. Up to an
inch of accumulation could occur in these locations with isolated
amounts of around 2" along some of the higher peaks.

Overall travel impacts should be minimal. Recent warm temperatures
should keep roadways mostly clear, though care should be had on
bridges and overpasses, especially in elevated locations. For more
information or to report snowfall amounts at your location, please
visit www.weather.gov/atlanta.

* WHAT...Minor coastal flooding expected. Inundation of 2 to 2.5
feet above ground level is possible along shorelines and low-
lying coastal areas.

* WHERE...Portions of northwest and west central Washington.

* WHEN...From 5 AM to 11 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Minor coastal flooding due to tidal overflow is
expected around high tide. This may lead to flooding of
parking lots, parks, and roads, with only isolated road
closures expected.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inundation above ground level refers to the height above the Mean
Higher High Water (MHHW) level.

properties.areaDesc: Lake, FL; Volusia, FL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 26 at 8:53PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Deland affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Previous rainfall working through the basin will cause river levels
on the St. Johns at Deland to continue rising through Major Flood
Stage. The river is forecast to rise above its former record crest
this weekend, reaching 6.5 feet, where it is expected to linger into
early next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Deland...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Deland.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 5.3 feet, Major flooding occurs to many structures and
marinas along the river and in the Hontoon Island area.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM EST Thursday the stage was 6.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 PM EST Thursday was 6.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise through Major Flood
Stage, reaching 6.5 feet late this weekend. The river is then
forecast to remain steady through early next week.
- Flood stage is 4.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Friday morning at 1100 AM EST.

properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 26 at 8:43PM EST until November 27 at 7:00AM EST by NWS Gray ME
properties.description:
* WHAT...Freezing rain expected. Total ice accumulations around one
tenth of an inch.

* WHERE...Portions of south central, west central, and western Maine
and northern New Hampshire.

* WHEN...Until 7 AM EST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Difficult travel conditions are possible due to icy road
conditions. This is especially true on untreated side roads.
Although ice amounts will be light, the freezing rain is expected
to fall on cold bare pavement. This will lead to the potential for
glaze ice formation on untreated roads, leading to dangerous travel
conditions.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. The latest road conditions
can be obtained at newengland511.org.

Be prepared for slippery roads. Slow down and use caution while
driving. If you are going outside, watch your first few steps taken
on stairs, sidewalks, and driveways. These surfaces could be icy and
slippery, increasing your risk of a fall and injury.

properties.areaDesc: Wayne; McCreary; Whitley
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 26 at 8:26PM EST by NWS Jackson KY
properties.description:
Rain will mix with or change to snow tonight. Temperatures will be
marginal for snow accumulation, and with the ground being warm, it
will further limit the potential. However, on the taller ridges
where temperatures will be the coldest, localized accumulations
around an inch may occur, mainly on grass or elevated surfaces.
This could allow for slushy accumulation on roads at times, mainly
bridges.

Any precipitation lingering into Friday should change back to
rain.

properties.areaDesc: Bell; Harlan; Letcher
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 26 at 8:26PM EST by NWS Jackson KY
properties.description:
Rain will mix with or change to snow tonight and continue into
Friday. Light snow accumulations of 1 to 3 inches are expected at
elevations mainly above 2,000 feet. This could lead to slick roads
at those higher elevations. Any accumulationS in valleys are
likely to be less than an inch and confined to grass and elevated
surfaces.

Use caution if traveling across the higher elevations tonight and
Friday.

* WHERE...Big Island Summits.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 26 at 7:55PM EST until November 27 at 3:00AM EST by NWS Mount Holly NJ
properties.description:
* WHAT...One to two feet of inundation above ground level in low-
lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Atlantic, Cape May, Atlantic Coastal Cape May, Coastal
Atlantic and Southeastern Burlington.

* WHEN...Until 3 AM EST Friday.

* IMPACTS...At this level, widespread roadway flooding occurs in
coastal and bayside communities and along inland tidal
waterways. Many roads become impassable. Some damage to
vulnerable structures may begin to occur. At this level,
flooding begins on the most vulnerable roads in coastal and
bayside communities, and along inland tidal waterways. Some
partial or full road closures are possible.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Warning means that moderate or major tidal
flooding is occurring or imminent. Be prepared for rising water
levels and take appropriate action to protect life and property.
Follow the recommendations of local emergency management
officials.

Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The water may be
deeper than you think it is. You will be putting yourself in
danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to costly
repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Warning means that moderate or major tidal
flooding is occurring or imminent. Be prepared for rising water
levels and take appropriate action to protect life and property.
Follow the recommendations of local emergency management
officials.

Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The water may be
deeper than you think it is. You will be putting yourself in
danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to costly
repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 26 at 7:28PM EST by NWS Louisville KY
properties.description:
Rain has begun to mix with and change to snow across portions of
south central and southeast Kentucky. Temperatures have fallen
into the low-to-mid 30s as well, with light snow accumulations
starting to be observed along and south of the Cumberland Parkway.
Additional light snow accumulations up to an inch will be
possible on grassy surfaces and elevated surfaces. Mild ground
temperatures should limit impacts to roadways. Snow should begin
to taper as precipitation rates decrease early Friday morning.

currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Collier County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Statement, through Friday
morning. For the High Rip Current Risk, through Friday
afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Some water on low lying roads and property. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Do not drive through flooded roadways.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Tidal overflow flooding.

* WHERE...South Washington Coast.

* WHEN...Until 5 PM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding, up to one foot above ground level,
during high tides is expected in the low lying areas near bays,
sloughs, and the lower reaches of the coastal rivers.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...For the South Washington Coast, total tides
at Toke Point will be 11.5 feet at 2 PM PST Friday November 27.

expected. Coastal residents in the warned area should be alert
for rising water, and take appropriate action to protect life and
property.

properties.areaDesc: North Bay Interior Valleys; San Francisco Bay Shoreline
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 26 at 3:35PM PST until November 29 at 5:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 1.7 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Bayshore locations along San Pablo and San Francisco
Bays.

* WHEN...Until 5 PM PST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.7 ft above normal (7.5 ft MLLW) at 12:31 PM
Friday, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 1:28 PM Saturday,
and 0.9 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) at 2:32 PM Sunday. These
predictions include up to 1.3 ft of surge that will enhance the
astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90
minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the
San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore; San Francisco Peninsula Coast; Northern Monterey Bay
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 26 at 3:35PM PST until November 28 at 4:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.7 ft of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards
Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip
currents with breaking waves of 13 to 19 ft.

* WHERE...The Pacific Coast.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST
Saturday. For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Friday
evening.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning,
pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.7 ft above normal (7.5 ft MLLW) at 12:31 PM
Friday, 1.6 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 1:28 PM Saturday,
and 0.9 ft above normal (6.8 ft MLLW) at 2:32 PM Sunday. These
predictions include up to 1.3 ft of surge that will enhance the
astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90
minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the
San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

properties.areaDesc: Mason, WA
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 26 at 3:17PM PST until November 27 at 3:34PM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Washington...

Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast to continue. This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...Until Friday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 17.5 feet, the Skokomish River will cause moderate
flooding, with deep and quick flood waters inundating some
residential areas, many roads, and much of the farm land in the
Skokomish Valley. Inundated roads include the Skokomish Valley
road, Bourgault Road West, Purdy Cutoff Road, and Highway 106.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:30 PM PST Thursday the stage was 17.9 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 2:30 PM PST Thursday was 17.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to continue to hover near a
crest of 17.9 feet through this evening. It will then fall below
flood stage tomorrow morning.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. Most flood related deaths occur
in automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips,
or low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at midnight PST.

* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, two to three feet of
inundation above ground level in vulnerable areas near the
waterfront and shoreline. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up
to one half foot of inundation above ground level expected in
vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline.

* WHERE...In Connecticut, Southern Fairfield and Southern New
Haven Counties. In New York, Southern Westchester, Bronx,
Northwest Suffolk, Northern Queens and Northern Nassau
Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 6 AM EST Friday.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 6 AM to 3 PM EST Friday.

* COASTAL FLOOD IMPACTS...Widespread moderate flooding of
vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline, including
roads, parking lots, parks, lawns, and homes and businesses
with basements near the waterfront. Numerous road closures are
likely, and vehicles parked in vulnerable areas near the
waterfront will likely become flooded. Minor to moderate
flooding will also extend well inland from the waterfront
along tidal rivers and bays, including up the Hudson River
into the Mid-Hudson Valley.

* SHORELINE IMPACTS...Large breaking waves of 3 to 7 ft will
result in areas of dune erosion and localized overwashes. Wave
splashover will exacerbate flooding of roadways and vulnerable
structures behind protective dunes and seawalls. There is
potential for scattered damage to shoreline and marina
structures as well.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

properties.areaDesc: Columbia River Bar
properties.headline: Hazardous Seas Warning issued November 26 at 12:39PM PST until November 27 at 1:00AM PST by NWS Portland OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Hazardous Seas Warning, very steep and
hazardous seas 14 to 15 ft at 13 seconds and southwest winds
15 to 25 kt. For the Small Craft Advisory, Rough bar
conditions expected.

* WHERE...In the Main Channel of the Columbia River Bar.

* WHEN...Hazardous Seas Warning, until 1 AM PST Friday. Small
Craft Advisory, from 1 AM Friday to 1 AM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Very steep and hazardous seas could capsize or cause
damage to vessels.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Very strong ebb current of 7.19 kt at 534
PM Thursday. Seas 15 to 18 ft. Ebb current of 3.46 kt at 617 AM
Friday. Seas 14 ft. Very strong ebb current of 6.75 kt at 625
PM Friday. Seas 15 ft.
properties.instruction:
A Hazardous Seas Warning means hazardous sea conditions are
imminent or occurring. Recreational boaters should remain in
port, or take shelter until waves subside.  Commercial vessels
should prepare for rough seas and consider remaining in port or
taking shelter in port until hazardous seas subside.

properties.areaDesc: Mecklenburg, VA
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 26 at 3:25PM EST by NWS Wakefield VA
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Wakefield has issued a Flood
Warning for the following rivers in Virginia...

Allen Creek near Boydton affecting Mecklenburg County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring.

* WHERE...Allen Creek near Boydton.

* WHEN...From this afternoon until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 16.5 feet, Hayes Mill Road begins to flood about 100
Feet east of Allen Creek.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:30 PM EST Thursday the stage was 15.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 13.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 2:30 PM EST Thursday was 15.3 feet.
- Forecast...No forecast is available for this location.
- Flood stage is 15.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 15.4
feet on 02/04/2016.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 330 AM EST.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Northeast winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 50 mph.

* WHERE...Erie, Lucas, Ottawa, Sandusky, and Wood Counties.

* WHEN...Until 3 AM EST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.
properties.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

properties.areaDesc: Yukon Delta Coast
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 26 at 11:20AM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
Periods of snow become increasingly likely through Thursday as a
front approaches the coast. Southeast winds gusting up to 35 mph
shift southerly and peak up to 40 mph late Friday. The
combination of falling snow and strong winds are expected to lead
to periods of reduced visibility due to blowing snow, with
visibilities falling to 1 mile or less at times. Total snow
accumulations of 1 to 3 inches expected through Friday night. The
heaviest snow is expected near Cape Romanzof including Chevak,
Hooper Bay, and Scammon Bay.

properties.areaDesc: St Lawrence Island
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 26 at 11:20AM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
Periods of snow are likely Thursday and Friday with southeast
winds gusting up to 45 mph. This will likely result in lowered
visibility to 1 mile or less at times. Temperatures will be
hovering near 32 degrees which means blowing snow will only be
expected when it is actively snowing. Total snow accumulations
around 1 to 3 inches expected through Friday evening.

properties.areaDesc: Eastern Beaufort Sea Coast
properties.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued November 26 at 10:33AM AKST until November 27 at 10:00PM AKST by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Periods of blizzard conditions. Winds gusting as high as 45
mph.

* WHERE...Point Thompson.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM AKST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Areas of blowing snow could significantly reduce
visibility.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Very little additional falling snow is
expected. Strong winds will blow snow already on the ground to
create areas of low visibility near the surface. No significant
visibility reductions are expected at Barter Island/Kaktovik due to
open water limiting the availability of blowable snow to the east.
properties.instruction:
If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, and water in your
vehicle in case of an emergency.

* WHERE...Central and Eastern Beaufort Sea Coast.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM AKST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Areas of blowing snow could significantly reduce
visibility.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Very little additional falling snow is

properties.instruction:

southern portions of the east TN mountains and southwest NC.

expected at times. While minor snowfall accumulations are
possible, and may lead to slick roads, the main impact is expected
to be due to reduced visibilities.

properties.areaDesc: Mason, WA
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 26 at 4:34AM PST until November 27 at 9:27AM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
...Forecast flooding changed from Moderate to Major severity for the
following rivers in Washington...

Skokomish River At Potlatch affecting Mason County.

.Heavy rain over the Olympics overnight with snow levels well above
mountain tops has driven the Skokomish River to major flood stage
this morning.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is
forecast. This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...Skokomish River at Potlatch.

* WHEN...Until Friday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 18.0 feet, the Skokomish River will cause major, near
record flooding throughout the Skokomish Valley. Deep and swift
flood waters will inundate residential areas, many roads including
SR 106, and much of the farm land.   Flooding will occur all along
the river including headwaters, tributaries, and other streams
within and near the Skokomish River Basin.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 3:30 AM PST Thursday the stage was 17.97 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 3:30 AM PST Thursday was 17.97 feet.
- Forecast...The river will rise to 18.1 feet late this morning. It
will then fall below flood stage on Friday morning. Further rises
through the weekend are likely, with exceeding flood stage
possible.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 17.8
feet on 03/19/1997.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Flooding is occurring or is imminent. Most flood related deaths occur
in automobiles. Do not attempt to cross water covered bridges, dips,
or low water crossings. Never try to cross a flowing stream, even a
small one, on foot. To escape rising water find another route over
higher ground.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this afternoon at 1245 PM PST.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 3 to 7
feet expected in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Pinellas, Coastal Hillsborough, Coastal Manatee,
Coastal Sarasota, Coastal Charlotte and Coastal Lee Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Friday evening.
For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 PM EST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 26 at 2:14AM EST until November 28 at 3:00AM EST by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Walton, Bay, Gulf, and Franklin County Beaches.

* WHEN...Through late Friday night.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Yuma, AZ
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 25 at 2:07PM MST until November 30 at 3:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by an upstream dam release is expected.

* WHERE...Central Yuma County in southwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 300 PM MST Monday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are
likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 202 PM MST, a streamflow gauge near Dateland continues to
steadily rise and is now showing a depth of just above 7.5 feet
with flow around 1250 cfs. This gauge is forecasted to reach
action stage (8 ft) on Friday. Flooding is expected along the
Gila River within the warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.
